title.purpose: Panel, day, station, rail and card titles (16-22px).

body.purpose: Prose, client names, ledes; ledes cap at 62-66ch.

data.purpose: References, codes, dates, money, inputs, buttons, chips; tabular numerals.

money-total.purpose: Payable figure on chrome, in accent-on-dark.

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels and column heads.

shadows.name: scroll-edge
shadows.purpose: Overflow cue on the horizontally scrolling lines table.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Station pip state changes (0.4s) and the new-job reveal (0.42s).

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Button, input, chip colour and border transitions.

motion.name: row-hover
motion.purpose: Docket row hover and delete-button reveal.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: st-reveal 0.42s: opacity 0, translateY(-6px), clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to rest

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Applied to everything under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Queue chips become a horizontal scroller; hub actions go full width.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Docket rows become two-column cards; column head hides; table scroll hint shows.

breakpoints.name: rail
breakpoints.purpose: Duty rail drops below the main column and stops sticking.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: Vessel column drops from the docket grid.

drift: Dashboard, Clients, Log, Courier, and the shared TopNav still use older inline styles from components/courier/tokens.ts and styles/workbench.css: paper #F6F3EE, chrome #111318, amber #C65911. Not repaired.
HsClassifyCell (src/pages/HsClassifyCell.tsx), embedded in the lines table, is a legacy inline-styled component: Fraunces 13px in its input and courier-token colours inside the .st world.
src/index.css global type layer forces font-weight 600 on every input, select, textarea, and button under #root, including .st controls.

narrative.overview:
The Stallion declarations world reads like a harbour-office ledger: near-black chrome bands frame warm paper sheets, and every job is filed under the day its goods land. Near-black is the frame, paper is the working surface, and burnt orange is the single ember that says "act here". Forest green says "done". Nothing else carries hue except the status vocabulary.

Density is operational, not airy. Rows are 58px tall, panels pad at 22px, labels are small uppercase mono, and every reference, code, and figure is set in tabular JetBrains Mono so columns of money align. Fraunces carries headings only: the page title, step titles, panel titles, day names, station names. Instrument Sans carries prose. The pairing is fixed by Stallion's brand commitment (PRODUCT.md) and must not drift toward another family.

The signature is the station track: four pips joined by hairlines, green when done, orange when current, hollow otherwise. It appears small in each docket row and full-size as the sticky, clickable station rail inside a job. Problems surface first and in place: blocking fields flag their own label and border rather than raising a separate alert surface.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black chrome bands (top bar, job bar, day rules, duty rail, XML preview) over a warm paper canvas.
One accent: burnt orange for the primary action, current station, today marker, focus ring, and "needed" flags.
Forest green only for done and receipted states.
Monospace for anything countable or codable; Fraunces only for headings; Instrument Sans for prose.
Flat: depth comes from tonal paper layers and 1px warm-grey rules, never drop shadows.
Squared, editorial corners (3-6px); the only full pill is the queue chip.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Burnt orange is the only accent. It marks exactly one thing per context: the primary action, where the job is now, today, or what is needed. Status hues (amber, red) appear only inside status chips, counts, flags, and banners, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Green Means Done Rule
rules.body: Forest green is reserved for completed stations, approved and receipted states, and relief. Never use it for links, selection, or emphasis.

rules.name: The Chrome Frames, Paper Works Rule
rules.body: Near-black is for bands that frame or summarize (top bar, job bar, day rules, duty rail, code). Editable content always sits on paper, sheet, or field.

rules.name: The Countable Is Mono Rule
rules.body: If it can be counted, keyed, or matched against a document (reference, HS code, BL, date, amount, status), it is JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals. Prose inputs opt out explicitly.

rules.name: The Serif Is For Headings Rule
rules.body: Fraunces is used only for headings and names of places in the route (stations, days, panels). Never in inputs, tables, or labels.

rules.name: The Flat Docket Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. If something needs to stand out, change its ground (sheet to chrome) or its rule weight, not its shadow.

dos: Do keep burnt orange to one role per context: primary action, current station, today, or needed.
Do set references, codes, dates, and money in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals, right-aligned in columns.
Do use Ember Ink (accent-ink) for orange text on paper and Ember on Dark (accent-on-dark) for orange text on chrome; reserve Burnt Ember itself for fills, rules, pips, and focus.
Do flag problems on the field itself (label colour, flag word, border, fill) and list them first in the checklist, blocking before "to check".
Do reuse the station track wherever a job's progress is shown.
Do separate surfaces with 1px Hairline rules and tonal steps (paper, sheet, field).
Do honour reduced motion; every transition and reveal collapses to near-zero duration.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to panels, rows, or cards; the system is flat.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or use amber and red outside status chips, counts, flags, and banners.
Don't use green for anything that is not done, approved, receipted, or relief.
Don't set Fraunces in inputs, table cells, or labels.
Don't put a mono label above a Fraunces heading as an eyebrow or kicker; headings stand alone, and uppercase mono labels name fields, columns, and field groups only.
Don't build a stat-card row or a zebra-striped status table for the hub; jobs are grouped by arrival day.
Don't round containers past 6px or use pills for anything but queue chips.
